content.value_statement: Complex backend systems can become tightly coupled and hard to test. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through proven architecture patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Clean Architecture layers and dependency direction.
Shows ports and adapters for Hexagonal Architecture.
Describes DDD entities, value objects, aggregates, and events.
Provides sample backend structure for repositories, controllers, and use cases.
Highlights best practices and common pitfalls for architecture decisions.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete generated application.
Examples are Python oriented and may need adaptation for other stacks.
It does not evaluate current production code without additional project context.
It does not replace detailed domain modeling with stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Backend Service
use_cases.description: Define layers, ports, adapters, and domain boundaries before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Coupled Application
use_cases.description: Separate business rules from controllers, databases, and external services.

use_cases.title: Create Team Architecture Standards
use_cases.description: Document patterns, naming conventions, and boundaries for shared backend work.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture-patterns skill to compare Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and DDD for my backend service. Recommend one pattern and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Design the Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture-patterns skill to design the layers, folders, and dependency rules for a service that handles users, orders, and payments.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactoring plan for a coupled backend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture-patterns skill to create a refactoring plan that moves business logic out of controllers and database adapters.

prompt_templates.title: Model Domain Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced DDD planning across multiple business areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture-patterns skill to identify bounded contexts, aggregates, value objects, repositories, and domain events for this product domain.

output_examples.input: Design a backend architecture for a payment and order workflow.
output_examples.output: A layered design with domain models, use cases, payment ports, repository adapters, and notification boundaries.

output_examples.input: Refactor a controller that validates orders, charges cards, and writes database rows.
output_examples.output: A migration plan that moves business rules into use cases and hides infrastructure behind ports.

output_examples.input: Define DDD building blocks for customer accounts and orders.
output_examples.output: A domain model proposal with aggregates, value objects, repository boundaries, and domain events.

best_practices: Start from domain behavior before choosing frameworks or storage tools.
Keep dependency direction explicit and test core logic without infrastructure.
Use small interfaces that match real use cases and team language.
anti_patterns: Putting business rules inside controllers, jobs, or database adapters.
Creating many layers for simple CRUD systems without clear benefit.
Sharing database models directly across unrelated bounded contexts.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when designing a backend service, refactoring coupling, or defining architecture standards.

faq.question: Does it generate a full application?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and planning guidance that you adapt to your codebase.

faq.question: Which patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Clean Architecture, Hexagonal Architecture, and tactical Domain-Driven Design patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline steps to separate domain logic from controllers, databases, and external services.

faq.question: Is it specific to Python?
faq.answer: The examples use Python, but the architecture concepts apply to most backend languages.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation only and does not require external services to run.
